Female sea turtles return to the very beach where they were born to lay their eggs, using Earth's magnetic field as their guide.

Paano nahahanap ng pawikan ang tamang dalampasigan?

Bumabalik ang mga babaeng pawikan sa mismong dalampasigang pinanganakan nila para mangitlog, ginagamit ang magnetic field ng Lupa bilang gabay.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkaplag sa pawikan sa hustong baybayon?

Mobalik ang babaye nga pawikan sa mismong baybayon diin sila natawo aron magitlog, gigamit ang magnetic field sa Yuta isip giya.

copy.tl: Sa ilalim ng mga tinik ng tihik ay may matigas at bilog na balat na tinatawag na 'test'. Ito ang naiiwan kapag namatay na ito at nalaglag ang mga tinik.
copy.bis: Sa ilawom sa mga tunok sa tihik adunay gahi ug lingin nga bagol nga gitawag og 'test'. Kini ang mahibilin kon mamatay na kini ug matangtang ang mga tunok.

Can a seahorse look two ways at once?

Yes! A seahorse's two eyes can move separately, so it can look in two different directions at the same time.
copy.tl:
Kayang tumingin ba ng seahorse sa dalawang direksyon?

Oo! Ang dalawang mata ng seahorse ay gumagalaw nang magkahiwalay, kaya nakakatingin ito sa dalawang direksyon nang sabay.
copy.bis:
Makatan-aw ba ang seahorse sa duha ka direksyon dungan?

Oo! Ang duha ka mata sa seahorse makalihok nga magkalahi, mao nga makatan-aw kini sa duha ka direksyon dungan.

Is a seahorse really a tiny horse?

Nope! A seahorse is actually a fish — only its head looks like a horse's, which is how it got its name.
copy.tl:
Totoo bang kabayo ang seahorse?

Hindi pala! Isda talaga ang seahorse — ang ulo lang nito ang kahawig ng kabayo, kaya nga tinawag itong kabayong-dagat.
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga kabayo ang seahorse?

Dili diay! Usa gyud ka isda ang seahorse — ang ulo ra niini ang morag kabayo, mao nga gitawag kining kabayong-dagat.

copy.tl: Lumalaki ang diameter ng puno taon-taon dahil sa secondary growth — ang vascular cambium ang nagdaragdag ng bagong xylem at phloem, kaya nabubuo ang mga singsing sa puno.
copy.bis: Nagkadaghan ang diameter sa kahoy matag tuig tungod sa secondary growth — ang vascular cambium ang nagdugang og bag-ong xylem ug phloem, mao nga natukod ang mga singsing sa punoan.

Ang limestone at sandstone! Marami tayong limestone formations sa Pilipinas, tulad ng mga bundok-apog sa Bohol at Palawan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mga pananglitan sa sedimentary rock?

Ang limestone ug sandstone! Daghan ta'g limestone formations sa Pilipinas, sama sa mga bukid-apog sa Bohol ug Palawan.

Why does a coconut float on the sea?

Its thick, fibrous husk is full of tiny air pockets. That trapped air keeps it from sinking, so it can travel across the sea!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang niyog sa dagat?

Ang makapal na bunot nito ay puno ng maliliit na bulsa ng hangin. Ang hangin na ito ang pumipigil dito na lumubog, kaya kayang maglakbay sa dagat!
copy.bis:
Nganong molutaw ang lubi sa dagat?

Ang baga nga bunot sa lubi puno sa gagmay nga puyo sa hangin. Kini nga hangin ang mopugong sa paglugdang, mao nga makabiyahe kini sa dagat!

copy.bis: Kaniadto, panulat ug papel ang gigamit sa seismograph, apan karon kadaghanan digital na! Ang electronic sensor nagpadala og datos sa computer, mao nga mas paspas ug tukma ang pagbasa.

copy.tl: Gumagalaw ang lupa paitaas-pababa AT patagilid! Kaya tatlong seismograph ang nagtutulungan—isa para sa pataas-pababa, dalawa para sa magkaibang gilid—para makuha ang buong galaw ng lindol.
copy.bis: Molihok ang yuta pataas-paubos UG patakilid! Mao nga tulo ka seismograph ang nagtinabangay—usa alang sa pataas-paubos, duha alang sa lainlaing kilid—aron makuha ang tibuok paglihok sa linog.

It must be fixed to solid rock so it moves with the real earthquake, not from wind or a passing truck!
copy.tl:
Bakit nakakabit nang mahigpit ang seismograph sa lupa?

Nakakabit ito sa matibay na bato para gumalaw lang sa tunay na lindol, hindi dahil sa hangin o dumadaang trak!
copy.bis:
Nganong lig-on nga nakakabit ang seismograph sa yuta?

Gikabit kini sa gahi nga bato aron molihok lang sa tinuod nga linog, dili tungod sa hangin o naglabay nga trak!

In selective breeding, people choose which animals or plants reproduce based on traits they like — that's how we got many dog breeds and corn types.
copy.tl:

Sa selective breeding, pinipili ng tao kung aling hayop o halaman ang magpaparami batay sa katangiang gusto nila — kaya nagkaroon tayo ng iba't ibang lahi ng aso at mais.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang selective breeding?

Sa selective breeding, ang tawo magpili kon unsang hayop o tanom ang magsanay base sa kinaiya nga gusto nila — mao nga aduna kitay lainlaing rasa sa iro ug mais.

What are the 5 senses?

The 5 senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.

Ano ang 5 pandama?

Ang 5 pandama ay paningin, pandinig, pang-amoy, panlasa, at pandama (hipo).
copy.bis:
Unsa ang 5 ka igbalati?

Ang 5 ka igbalati mao ang panan-aw, pandungog, pang-simhot, pang-tilaw, ug paghikap.

Yes! Sharks are super ancient — they were already swimming in the sea even before the dinosaurs appeared.

Oo! Napakatanda na ng mga pating — may pating na sa dagat bago pa man dumating ang mga dinosaur.
copy.bis:

Oo! Karaan na kaayo ang mga iho — may iho na sa dagat bisan sa wala pa moabot ang mga dinosaur.

Why is shark skin rough?

It feels like sandpaper because it's covered in tiny, sharp scales.
copy.tl:
Bakit magaspang ang balat ng pating?

Parang lija ito dahil natatakpan ng maliliit na matalim na kaliskis.

Nganong gaspang ang panit sa pating?

Morag lija kini tungod kay natabonan sa gagmayng hait nga himbis.

copy.bis: Lain-laing gidak-on ang iho — ang uban gamay ra sama sa imong bukton, ang uban dako kaayo — ug ang hammerhead shark adunay talagsaon nga ulo nga porma martilyo nga may mata sa matag tumoy!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes cilia on gills creating a feeding current, but cilia on gills are not the outer body parts (head, legs, wings) that G3-L-4 targets, and the content is too specialized for this grade-3 competency.

copy.en:
How does a shellfish eat without hands?

It uses countless tiny hairs called cilia on its gills, beating nonstop to create a current that pulls water in!
copy.tl:
Paano kumakain ang kabibe kung walang kamay?

Gumagamit ito ng napakaraming maliliit na buhok na tinatawag na cilia sa hasang nito, na patuloy na gumagalaw para lumikha ng agos ng tubig papasok!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagkaon sa kabibe nga walay kamot?

Naggamit kini og daghang gagmayng balhibo nga gitawag og cilia sa iyang hasang, nga padayong molihok aron mohimo og sulog sa tubig pasulod!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mussels cling tight to rocks and posts using strong threads
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes mussel byssus threads used for attachment, not an outer body part such as head, legs, or wings, and the role is clinging rather than moving or gathering food.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal structure but does not describe an evolutionary adaptation such as mimicry or camouflage, nor does it use secondary sources to explain how the animal changed to suit its environment.

copy.en: Mussels cling tight to rocks and posts using strong threads that they make themselves!
copy.tl: Kumakapit nang mahigpit ang tahong sa bato o poste gamit ang matitibay na sinulid na sarili nilang ginagawa!
copy.bis: Ang tahong nanapot og lig-on sa bato o poste pinaagi sa lig-on nga hilo nga sila mismo ang naghimo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An oyster doesn't chase its food; it stays put while the water brings food to it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how an oyster obtains food without moving, but does not describe any outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement or food gathering as required by the competency.

copy.en: An oyster doesn't chase its food; it stays put while the water brings food to it.
copy.tl: Hindi naghahabol ng pagkain ang talaba; naghihintay lang ito habang dinadala ng tubig ang pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang talaba dili manggukod og pagkaon; naghulat lang kini samtang ang tubig magdala sa pagkaon ngadto niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Shivering for a long time burns up a lot of energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions shivering, which involves muscles, but it does not describe how the muscular system (or any other listed system) works. It only states that shivering uses energy, which is a fact about energy expenditure, not an explanation of the muscular system's function or mechanism.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: burns up a lot of energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions energy being used, but it does not identify energy as something that can cause change, nor does it address light, sound, or heat energy. It only states that shivering consumes energy, which is not the same as the competency's focus on energy causing change.

copy.en:
Why do you feel tired after shivering a lot?

Shivering for a long time burns up a lot of energy, which is why it can leave you feeling tired and hungry afterward.
copy.tl:
Bakit ka napapagod pagkatapos manginig nang matagal?

Ang matagal na panginginig ay gumagamit ng maraming enerhiya, kaya nakakapagod at nakakagutom ito.
copy.bis:
Ngano ka mokapoy human pagkurog og dugay?

Ang dugay nga pagkurog mogamit og daghang kusog, mao nga makapakapoy ug makapagutom kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Migratory shorebirds usually arrive in the Philippines from October to March
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the seasonal arrival of migratory shorebirds, a behavioral pattern, but does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment (e.g., mimicry or camouflage). It shares the broad subject of animals and environment but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: while it's winter up north
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions winter in the north as a reason for migration, touching on seasons, but it does not describe the different seasons in the Philippines or suggest activities appropriate for each season. The focus is on shorebird arrival timing, not Philippine seasons or seasonal activities.

copy.en:
When do migratory shorebirds arrive in the Philippines?

Migratory shorebirds usually arrive in the Philippines from October to March, while it's winter up north.
copy.tl:
Kailan dumarating ang mga lumilipat na ibong dagat sa Pilipinas?

Karaniwang dumarating ang mga lumilipat na ibong dagat sa Pilipinas mula Oktubre hanggang Marso, habang taglamig sa hilaga.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a moabot ang mga balhinong langgam sa baybayon sa Pilipinas?

Kasagaran moabot ang mga balhinong langgam sa baybayon sa Pilipinas gikan Oktubre hangtod Marso, samtang tingtugnaw sa amihanan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hydrocarbons with short carbon chains are light and boil at low temperatures!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions boiling at low temperatures, which is a state change, but it does not describe how temperature changes cause matter to change state in general. It focuses on a specific property of hydrocarbons (boiling point) rather than the process of state change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: That is why they become the gases and gasoline collected near the top.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to gases and gasoline collecting near the top, which hints at separation by boiling point (fractional distillation), but it does not demonstrate any of the listed separation techniques (decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, magnets). The connection to separation is indirect and not instructional.

copy.en:
Why do gases and gasoline collect near the top?

Hydrocarbons with short carbon chains are light and boil at low temperatures! That is why they become the gases and gasoline collected near the top.
copy.tl:
Bakit ang gases at gasoline ay nagtitipon sa itaas?

Ang mga hydrocarbons na may maiikling carbon chains ay magaan at kumukulo sa mababang temperatura! Kaya sila ang nagiging gases at gasoline sa itaas.
copy.bis:
Nganong ang mga gas ug gasolina nagtipon sa taas?

Ang mga hydrocarbons nga adunay mubo nga carbon chains mga gaan ug mobukal sa ubos nga temperatura! Busa sila ang mga gas ug gasolina sa taas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a shorter string part always makes a higher pitch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses pitch variation with string length, which is a property of sound, but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a shorter string part always makes a higher pitch
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions pitch but does not use scientific wave terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, or velocity, nor does it involve research from secondary sources. It only touches on a sound property without the required terminology or research activity.

copy.en: Thickness changes the sound, but length matters too! No matter how thick it is, a shorter string part always makes a higher pitch.
copy.tl: Nakakaapekto ang kapal, pero ang haba ay napakahalaga rin! Kahit gaano kapál, ang mas maikling bahagi ay laging gumagawa ng mas mataas na tunog.
copy.bis: Naka-apekto ang gibag-on, pero importante sad ang gitas-on! Bisan unsa kabaga, ang mas mubong bahin kanunay mohimo ug mas taas nga tingog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A ukulele is smaller and has shorter strings than a guitar. That is why it sounds higher and brighter compared to the deeper sound of a guitar!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why a ukulele has a higher pitch than a guitar based on string length, but it does not describe how sound is made (e.g., vibration) or transferred (e.g., through air). It only touches on the topic of sound without directly supporting the competency's focus on sound production and transfer.

copy.en: A ukulele is smaller and has shorter strings than a guitar. That is why it sounds higher and brighter compared to the deeper sound of a guitar!
copy.tl: Mas maliit ang ukulele at mas maiikli ang kuwerdas nito kaysa sa gitara. Kaya mas mataas at mas matinis ang tunog nito kumpara sa malalim na tunog ng gitara!
copy.bis: Mas gamay ang ukulele ug mas mubo ang kuwerdas niini kaysa sa gitara. Mao nga mas taas ug mas hayag ang tingog niini kumpara sa lawom nga tingog sa gitara!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so it can keep eating
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes shrew activity patterns and mentions eating, but does not teach the identification of basic needs (air, food, water, shelter). The food reference is incidental, not instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: A shrew never sleeps for long — it's active in short bursts all day and night so it can keep eating!
copy.tl: Hindi natutulog nang matagal ang shrew — aktibo ito sa maiikling sandali araw at gabi para palaging makakain!
copy.bis: Dili matulog og dugay ang shrew — aktibo kini sa mubo nga mga higayon adlaw ug gabii aron kanunay makakaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A shrew munches on insects, worms, and other tiny creatures it finds on the ground.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about a shrew's diet but does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources to do so. It provides no classification or comparison, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A shrew munches on insects, worms, and other tiny creatures it finds on the ground.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw a simple food chain using living things from the Philippines and label them as herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a Philippine animal and its food but does not draw a food chain or label any organism as herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore. The required drawn food chain with labels is absent, so the card does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: A shrew munches on insects, worms, and other tiny creatures it finds on the ground.
copy.tl: Kumakain ang shrew ng mga insekto, bulate, at iba pang maliliit na hayop na nahahanap nito sa lupa.
copy.bis: Mokaon ang shrew og mga insekto, ulod, ug uban pang gagmayng mananap nga makit-an niini sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People, dogs, and birds are warm-blooded
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People, dogs, and birds are warm-blooded — their body stays about the same warmth anywhere. But a shrimp is cold-blooded
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Warm-blooded versus cold-blooded is not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en: People, dogs, and birds are warm-blooded — their body stays about the same warmth anywhere. But a shrimp is cold-blooded, so its warmth changes with the water!
copy.tl: Mainit ang dugo ng tao, aso, at ibon — halos pareho lang ang init ng katawan nila kahit saan. Pero malamig ang dugo ng hipon, kaya nagbabago ang init nito ayon sa tubig!
copy.bis: Init og dugo ang tawo, iro, ug langgam — hapit managsama ra ang kainit sa ilang lawas bisan asa. Apan bugnaw og dugo ang hipon, mao nga mausab ang kainit niini sumala sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its two claws are so tiny you can barely feel them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a shrimp's claws (an outer body part) but does not describe their role in movement or gathering food, which is the focus of G3-L-4. It only addresses a misconception about pain, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Some kids think a shrimp pinches painfully like a crab, but its two claws are so tiny you can barely feel them!
copy.tl: Akala ng iba ay masakit manipit ang hipon gaya ng alimango, pero napakaliit ng dalawang sipit nito kaya halos hindi mo ito maramdaman!
copy.bis: Naghunahuna ang uban nga sakit moipit ang hipon sama sa alimango, apan gagmay kaayo ang duha ka sipit niini busa halos dili nimo mabati!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a long green chili that's only mildly spicy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a chili pepper, which is a living thing, but it does not address the difference between living and non-living things or give examples of each. It only provides a culinary description, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What is siling haba?

It's a long green chili that's only mildly spicy — perfect for adding flavor to sinigang!
copy.tl:
Ano ang siling haba?

Ito ay mahaba at berdeng sili na banayad lang ang anghang — sarap ipampasarap sa sinigang!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang siling haba?

Kini taas ug berde nga sili nga dili kaayo halang — maayong ilasa sa sinigang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When it dries out, it shrinks and wrinkles as the water leaves it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes water leaving a chili during drying, which is an everyday example of evaporation, but it does not name the change of state, nor does it use diagrams or flowcharts as required by the competency. It provides no direct instruction on melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation as state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fresh long green chili is mostly water inside
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water as a substance but does not identify the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or classify the chili/water into states. It does not support the skill of identifying that matter exists in three states.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When it dries out, it shrinks and wrinkles as the water leaves it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: Drying involves water changing from liquid to gas, but the card does not mention temperature as the cause, nor does it describe a change of state in terms of solid/liquid/gas. It only notes water leaving, without linking it to temperature-driven state change.

copy.en:
Why does chili shrink when it dries?

Fresh long green chili is mostly water inside, making it crunchy and juicy. When it dries out, it shrinks and wrinkles as the water leaves it.
copy.tl:
Bakit lumiliit ang siling haba kapag natuyo?

Ang sariwang siling haba ay halos puro tubig sa loob, kaya ito malutong at masustansya. Kapag natuyo na, lumiliit at kumukunot ito dahil nawawala ang tubig.
copy.bis:
Ngano nagkunhod ang siling haba kung mamala?

Ang lab-as nga siling haba halos puro tubig ang sulod, mao nga malutong ug masustansya kini. Kung mamala na, mokunhod ug mokulobot kini kay mawala ang tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fresh silk from the cocoon is usually white or slightly yellow!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the color of silk, which is a physical property, but the competency focuses on describing properties like hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not describe silk's hardness, shininess, or stretchability, nor does it frame color as a general physical property of solid materials. It is only tangentially related.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: To get colorful silk, it is dyed first before being made into clothing.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions dyeing silk, which is a change to a material, but the competency is about how changes like shaping, pressing, hammering, joining, or cutting make solid materials useful. Dyeing is not one of these changes, and the card does not explain how dyeing makes silk useful. It only states that dyeing is done to add color.

copy.en:
What color is silk when it first comes from the cocoon?

Fresh silk from the cocoon is usually white or slightly yellow! To get colorful silk, it is dyed first before being made into clothing.
copy.tl:
Anong kulay ng sutla kapag bagong kuha sa cocoon?

Ang bagong sutla mula sa cocoon ay karaniwang puti o medyo dilaw! Para magkaroon ng kulay, tinitina muna ito bago gawing damit.
copy.bis:
Unsay kolor sa sutla kung bag-ong kuha sa cocoon?

Ang bag-ong sutla gikan sa cocoon kasagaran puti o medyo dalag! Aron makakuha og kolor, tinaan una kini sa dili pa himoon nga sanina.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Silk clothing is light and keeps your body comfortable!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes silk clothing as light, comfortable, and temperature-regulating (warm when cold, cool when warm). The competency G3-M-5 asks students to describe physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. The card does not address hardness, shininess, stretchability, or any of the listed physical properties; it focuses on comfort and thermal insulation, which are not the targeted physical properties.

copy.en:
Why do people love wearing silk clothes?

Silk clothing is light and keeps your body comfortable! It warms you when it's cold, and stays cool during the warm season.
copy.tl:
Bakit gusto ng mga tao ang damit na sutla?

Ang damit na sutla ay magaan at komportable sa katawan! Nagpapainit ito kapag malamig, at hindi masyadong mainit kapag tag-init.
copy.bis:
Nganong ganahan mga tawo og sanina nga sutla?

Ang sanina nga sutla gaan ug komportable sa lawas! Makapainit kini kung tugnaw, ug dili kaayo init kung ting-init.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Spider silk is so strong and body-friendly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses spider silk as a biomedical material; it does not describe outer body parts of animals or their roles in movement and food gathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scientists study it for medicine — like dissolving stitches and healing scaffolds for wounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a biomedical application of spider silk, which could be seen as a science invention, but it does not use information from home or the local community, nor does it explain impact on everyday life in the required manner.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: scientists study it for medicine — like dissolving stitches and healing scaffolds for wounds
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the term biotechnology and provide examples
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a biomedical use of spider silk, but it does not explain the term biotechnology or provide a clear example of biotechnology as a field; the connection is too indirect.

copy.en: Spider silk is so strong and body-friendly that scientists study it for medicine — like dissolving stitches and healing scaffolds for wounds.
copy.tl: Napakatibay at biocompatible ng sutla ng gagamba kaya pinag-aaralan ito ng mga siyentipiko para sa medisina — tulad ng dissolving sutures at scaffold para sa paggaling ng sugat.
copy.bis: Lig-on ug biocompatible ang sutla sa lawalawa mao nga gitun-an kini sa mga siyentista para sa medisina — sama sa dissolving suture ug scaffold para sa pag-ayo sa samad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It resonates in the head, chest, and throat cavities!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses where a singer's voice resonates and that resonating spaces amplify frequencies, but it does not explain how sound is made or transferred. It is only tangentially about sound in an everyday situation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: These resonating spaces amplify certain frequencies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'frequencies' but does not describe wave properties using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, or velocity, nor does it involve research from secondary sources.

copy.en:
Where does a singer's voice resonate?

It resonates in the head, chest, and throat cavities! These resonating spaces amplify certain frequencies, giving the voice its distinctive quality.
copy.tl:
Saan nagre-resonate ang boses ng mang-aawit?

Sa mga cavity ng ulo, dibdib, at lalamunan! Ang mga resonating spaces na ito ay nag-a-amplify ng certain frequencies, kaya natatangi ang boses.
copy.bis:
Asa nag-resonate ang boses sa mag-aawit?

Sa mga cavity sa ulo, dughan, ug tutunlan! Kining mga resonating spaces nag-amplify sa certain frequencies, mao nga lahi ang kalidad sa boses.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sinkhole forms when a limestone underground cave grows too big and its roof collapses!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sinkholes as a natural landform, but G5-E-1 focuses on identifying local examples of landforms such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines and describing how they influence non-living and living components. Sinkholes are not among the listed examples, and the card only notes they are a hazard, without describing influence on non-living and living components in the manner required. This is same-subject background, not direct support.

copy.en: A sinkhole forms when a limestone underground cave grows too big and its roof collapses! They can appear suddenly, making them a hazard in karst limestone areas like Cebu and Bohol.
copy.tl: Ang sinkhole ay nabubuo kapag ang underground cave sa limestone ay naging masyadong malaki at bumagsak ang kisame! Lumilitaw sila nang bigla, kaya ito ay peligro sa mga karst limestone areas tulad ng Cebu at Bohol.
copy.bis: Ang sinkhole naporma kon ang underground cave sa limestone magdako kaayo ug mahulog ang kisame! Motungha sila nga biglaan, mao kini nga peligro sa mga karst limestone areas sama sa Cebu ug Bohol.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sinkhole is a sudden pit that forms when the ground collapses into a hollow space below!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines a sinkhole, which is a type of landform, but the competency requires identifying local examples of specific landforms (mountains, valleys, rivers, coastlines) and describing their influence on living and non-living components. The card provides no local examples and no discussion of environmental influence, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: A sinkhole is a sudden pit that forms when the ground collapses into a hollow space below!
copy.tl: Ang sinkhole ay isang biglang lubak na nabubuo kapag ang lupa ay gumuho papunta sa hungkag na espasyo sa ilalim!
copy.bis: Ang sinkhole usa ka biglang lungag nga maporma kon ang yuta mahugno paingon sa bakante nga luna sa ilawom!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An adult body usually has 206 bones — all working together to hold you up and let you move!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the number of bones and a general function, but does not describe how the skeletal system works in simple terms as required by the competency. It provides no explanation of bones, joints, support, protection, or movement mechanisms.

copy.en:
How many bones does a grown-up have?

An adult body usually has 206 bones — all working together to hold you up and let you move!
copy.tl:
Ilang buto mayroon ang isang matanda?

Karaniwang may 206 na buto ang katawan ng isang may sapat na gulang na tao — lahat ito nagtutulungan para itindig at maipagalaw ka!
copy.bis:
Pila ka bukog ang naa sa hamtong nga tawo?

Kasagaran adunay 206 ka bukog ang lawas sa hamtong nga tawo — nagtinabangay kini para makatindog ug makalihok ka!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's the femur, your thigh bone — the longest and strongest bone you have!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about the femur, a bone in the skeletal system, but does not describe how the skeletal system (or any body system) works. It provides no information about the function or operation of the system, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Which is the longest bone in your body?

It's the femur, your thigh bone — the longest and strongest bone you have!
copy.tl:
Alin ang pinakamahabang buto sa katawan?

Ito ang femur, ang buto ng hita — ang pinakamahaba at pinakamatibay na buto mo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakataas nga bukog sa lawas?

Kini ang femur, ang bukog sa paa — ang pinakataas ug pinakakusgan nga bukog nimo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Clothes work together with your skin to control body heat
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure

copy.en: Clothes work together with your skin to control body heat: thin, loose clothes let sweat and air escape on hot days, while thick clothes trap heat when it's cold.
copy.tl: Tinutulungan ng damit ang balat sa pagkontrol ng init: manipis at maluwag na damit ang tumutulong lumabas ang pawis at hangin sa mainit na araw, habang makapal na damit ang nagtatago ng init kapag malamig.
copy.bis: Gitabangan sa sinina ang panit sa pagkontrol sa kainit: nipis ug haluag nga sinina motabang mogawas ang singot ug hangin sa init nga adlaw, samtang baga nga sinina motago sa kainit kung tugnaw.

copy.en:
Why is no fingerprint the same?

The skin on your fingertips has one-of-a-kind patterns called fingerprints — no two people in the world have the same ones!
copy.tl:
Bakit walang magkaparehong bakas ng daliri?

Ang balat sa dulo ng mga daliri mo ay may natatanging guhit na tinatawag na bakas ng daliri — walang dalawang taong magkapareho!
copy.bis:
Nganong walay parehas nga fingerprint?

Ang panit sa tumoy sa imong mga tudlo adunay talagsaon nga marka nga gitawag og fingerprint — walay duha ka tawo nga managsama!

copy.en:
Do goosebumps mean you're sick?

Not by themselves! Goosebumps are usually just from cold or emotion. But if they come with shivering and a hot, feverish feeling, tell a parent so it can be checked.
copy.tl:
Tanda ba ng sakit ang goosebumps?

Hindi mismo! Karaniwang dulot lang ito ng lamig o damdamin. Pero kung kasabay nito ang panginginig at pakiramdam na mainit-init ang katawan, saka mo na lang sabihin sa magulang para suriin.
copy.bis:
Timailhan ba sa sakit ang goosebumps?

Dili mismo! Kasagaran kini gikan ra sa katugnaw o pagbati. Apan kung kuyog niini ang pagkurog ug init nga pamati sa lawas, ingna ang ginikanan aron masusi.

copy.en:
Is your skin just a plain cover?

No way! Your skin is alive and always busy — it feels, sweats, heals, and renews itself every day to protect you.
copy.tl:
Basta pantakip lang ba ang balat mo?

Hindi! Buhay at abala ang balat mo — nakakaramdam ito, pumapawis, gumagaling, at nagpapanibago araw-araw para bantayan ka.
copy.bis:
Tabon ra ba gyud ang panit nimo?

Dili gayod! Buhi ug okupado ang imong panit — makabati kini, mosingot, moayo, ug nagbag-o adlaw-adlaw aron panalipdan ka.

copy.en:
What's the body's biggest organ?

It's your skin! It covers about 1.7 square meters in an average adult — making it the largest organ in the whole body.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pinakamalaking organo ng katawan?

Ang balat mo! Sumasaklaw ito ng humigit-kumulang 1.7 metro kuwadrado sa isang karaniwang taong may sapat na gulang — pinakamalaking organo sa buong katawan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakadakong organ sa lawas?

Ang imong panit! Nagtabon kini ug mga 1.7 square meter sa usa ka kasagarang hamtong nga tawo — mao ang pinakadakong organ sa tibuok lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your skin is the biggest organ in your whole body!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes skin as an organ and sense of touch, but G4-L-1 specifically covers muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. Skin is not among these systems, and the card provides no information about how any of those systems work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's also what lets you feel things through touch.

assignedReviews.reason: Skin is an outer body part, but G3-L-4 focuses on parts like head, legs, or wings and their role in movement and gathering food. The card only mentions touch, not movement or food gathering, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: Your skin is the biggest organ in your whole body! It's also what lets you feel things through touch.
copy.tl: Ang balat mo ang pinakamalaking organ sa buong katawan! Ito rin ang ginagamit mo para maramdaman ang mga bagay sa pamamagitan ng hipo.
copy.bis: Ang imong panit mao ang pinakadako nga organ sa tibuok lawas! Kini usab ang gigamit nimo para mobati sa mga butang pinaagi sa paghikap.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your skin works like a sealed barrier around your body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes skin as a barrier, but G4-L-1 specifically covers the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. Skin is not among these systems, so the card does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its cells are packed so tightly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a labelled diagram to describe the connections between the levels of biological organization to one another from cells to the biosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions cells but does not use a labelled diagram to describe connections between levels of biological organization from cells to the biosphere. It only touches on the cellular level of skin, not the required diagram or the hierarchy of organization.

copy.en: Your skin works like a sealed barrier around your body — its cells are packed so tightly that germs and water can't easily get through, which is why healthy, unbroken skin helps keep you from getting sick.
copy.tl: Ang balat mo ay parang sealed na harang sa buong katawan — magkakadikit nang husto ang mga selula nito kaya hindi basta-basta makakapasok ang mikrobyo o tubig, kaya nga kapag buo ang balat mo, mas mahirap kang magkasakit.
copy.bis: Ang imong panit sama sa sirado nga babag sa tibuok lawas — hugot kaayo nga nagdikit ang mga selula niini mao nga lisod sudlon sa mikrobyo o tubig, mao nga kung wala maguba ang imong panit, lisod ka magsakit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: without its protective skin, germs sneak in easily and the body dries out fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that skin loss allows germs in and causes drying out, which touches on maintaining internal conditions, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or mention its indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure). It is background about skin's protective role, not direct instruction on homeostasis.

copy.en: A big burn means a hospital trip — without its protective skin, germs sneak in easily and the body dries out fast.
copy.tl: Kapag malaki ang paso, dinadala sa ospital ang pasyente — kapag nawala ang protektang balat, madaling pumasok ang mikrobyo at mabilis matuyot ang katawan.
copy.bis: Kung dako ang paso, dad-on sa ospital ang pasyente — kung mawala ang panalipod nga panit, dali mosulod ang mikrobyo ug paspas mauga ang lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: old cells on top dry up and flake off while new cells take over from below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that cells reproduce through two types of cell division, mitosis and meiosis, and describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes skin cell renewal, which is an outcome of mitosis, but it does not mention mitosis, meiosis, or the two types of cell division, nor does it describe mitosis as cell division for growth and repair. It only gives a specific example of cell replacement without connecting it to the competency's core concepts.

copy.en: Your body is always renewing its skin — old cells on top dry up and flake off while new cells take over from below.
copy.tl: Palaging nagpapalit ng balat ang iyong katawan — natutuyo at nalalaglag ang lumang selula sa ibabaw habang bagong selula ang humahalili mula sa ilalim.
copy.bis: Ang imong lawas kanunay nga mag-ilis sa panit — ang daan nga mga selula sa ibabaw mauga ug mangahulog samtang bag-ong selula ang mopuli gikan sa ilawom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the odor only appears when bacteria on your skin break it down
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: Naming bacteria is not recognizing unicellular versus multicellular organisms.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the odor only appears when bacteria on your skin break it down, especially in the armpits
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Skin bacteria breaking down sweat is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en:
Does sweat itself really smell bad?

Not really! Fresh sweat has almost no smell — the odor only appears when bacteria on your skin break it down, especially in the armpits.
copy.tl:
Talaga bang mabaho ang pawis mismo?

Hindi pala! Halos walang amoy ang sariwang pawis — lumalabas lang ang amoy kapag pinaghahalo ito ng bakteria sa balat, lalo na sa kilikili.
copy.bis:
Tinud-anay bang baho ang singot mismo?

Dili diay! Halos walay baho ang bag-ong singot — motungha lang ang baho kon dunoton kini sa bakterya sa panit, ilabina sa ilok.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bones and calcium absorption, which touches on the skeletal system, but it does not describe how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory system works. It is a nutrition/vitamin fact, not an explanation of a body system's function.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states a benefit of sunlight for vitamin D production, which is related to the Sun's importance to living things, but it does not make suggestions for a group/class discussion or confirm/record ideas from secondary sources. copy.en: Sunlight helps your skin make vitamin D from a type of cholesterol, and that vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium for strong bones.
copy.tl: Kapag nalantad sa sikat ng araw, gumagawa ang balat ng bitamina D mula sa isang uri ng cholesterol, at tumutulong ito sa katawan na masipsip ang calcium para sa matibay na buto.
copy.bis: Kung maladlad sa silaw sa adlaw, ang panit maghimo og bitamina D gikan sa usa ka klase sa cholesterol, ug kini nagtabang sa lawas nga mosuyop og calcium alang sa lig-on nga bukog.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a cost of tail loss (loss of stored energy) but does not describe how an animal has changed to better suit its environment, nor does it mention mimicry, camouflage, or any adaptive change. copy.en: A skink stores fat for energy in its tail, so dropping the tail has a cost — that saved food is lost and must be replaced.
copy.tl: Nakaimbak ng taba ang buntot ng skink na pinagkukunan ng enerhiya, kaya may kapalit ang paghulog nito — nawawala ang naipong pagkain at kailangan itong palitan.
copy.bis: Nagtago ang ikog sa skink og tambok nga gigikanan sa enerhiya, busa naay bayad ang pagpahulog niini — mawala ang natipon nga pagkaon ug kinahanglan pulihan.

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a light behavior (scattering) but does not support the grade 3 competency of participating in guided activities to explore sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and uses. copy.en: The sky looks blue because blue light from the sun scatters most easily in the air!
copy.tl: Asul ang langit dahil ang asul na liwanag mula sa araw ay pinakamadaling magkalat sa hangin!
copy.bis: Asul ang langit tungod kay ang asul nga kahayag gikan sa adlaw mao ang labing sayon nga magkatag sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When you don't get enough sleep, you feel tired and it's harder to think clearly.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an effect of sleep deprivation (tiredness, impaired thinking) but does not teach homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor mention its indicators such as body temperature, glucose level, or blood pressure.

assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address any of the named body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) or how they work; it concerns sleep and mental fatigue, which is outside the competency's scope.

copy.en: When you don't get enough sleep, you feel tired and it's harder to think clearly.
copy.tl: Kapag kulang sa tulog, nakakaramdam tayo ng pagod at nahihirapan tayong mag-isip nang maayos.
copy.bis: Kung kulang sa tulog, mobati ta og kapoy ug maglisod ta sa paghunahuna og tarong.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that regular sleep keeps the body strong and healthy, which is tangentially related to homeostasis, but it does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it mention indicators such as body temperature, glucose level, or blood pressure. copy.en: A child who is always short on sleep tends to get sick more often and tire out faster — enough, regular sleep keeps the body strong and healthy.
copy.tl: Ang batang laging kulang sa tulog ay mas madalas magkasakit at mas mabilis mapagod — ang sapat at regular na tulog ang nagpapanatiling malakas at malusog ng katawan.
copy.bis: Ang bata nga kanunay kulang sa tulog mas masagad magsakit ug mas dali makapoy — ang igo ug regular nga tulog ang magpabilin nga lig-on ug himsog sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some sloths have extra bones in their neck, which lets them turn their head almost all the way around
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an animal feature that could be an adaptation, but it does not describe how sloths have changed to better suit their environment or connect the neck bones to environmental pressure. It lacks the explanatory link to adaptation that the competency requires.

copy.en:
How can a sloth turn its head so far?

Some sloths have extra bones in their neck, which lets them turn their head almost all the way around — without moving their body at all!
copy.tl:
Paano kayang umikot nang husto ang ulo ng sloth?

May dagdag na buto sa leeg ang ilang sloth, kaya kaya nilang ilingon ang ulo nang halos buong ikot — kahit hindi gumagalaw ang katawan!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pag-ikot pag-ayo ang ulo sa sloth?

Ang ubang sloth adunay dugang bukog sa liog, mao nga makalingi sila sa ulo halos hingpit nga ikot — bisan wala molihok ang lawas!

copy.en:
Is a sloth really a kind of bear?

No! Even though it's sometimes casually called a bear, the sloth is actually a closer relative of the anteater, an ant-eating animal.
copy.tl:
Talaga bang oso ang sloth?

Hindi! Kahit minsang tinatawag itong bear, ang sloth ay mas malapit na kamag-anak ng anteater, isang hayop na kumakain ng langgam.
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga oso ang sloth?

Dili! Bisan usahay gitawag kini nga bear, ang sloth mas duol nga paryente sa anteater, usa ka mananap nga mokaon og hulmigas.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions claws as an outer body part but does not describe their role in movement or gathering food, which is the core of the competency. It also does not involve observing or describing body parts beyond a naming detail.

copy.en: There are two main kinds of sloth — two-toed and three-toed, named for the claws on their front feet. They look and move a bit differently, but both are slow and live in trees.
copy.tl: May dalawang pangunahing uri ng sloth — ang may dalawang daliri at ang may tatlong daliri sa unahang paa. Bahagyang magkaiba sila sa hitsura at galaw, pero pareho silang mabagal at nakatira sa puno.
copy.bis: Adunay duha ka nag-unang klase sa sloth — ang duha ka tudlo ug ang tulo ka tudlo sa atubangang tiil. Gamay silag kalainan sa hitsura ug paglihok, apan pareho silang hinay ug nagpuyo sa kahoy.

assignedReviews.reason: The card states a speed value for a sloth but does not explain that speed is how far an object moves in a given time. It provides an example of speed without teaching the concept or definition required by the competency.

copy.en:
Which mammal is the slowest?

The sloth! It moves at only about 0.24 kilometers per hour.
copy.tl:
Alin ang pinakamabagal na mammal?

Ang sloth! Gumagalaw lang ito nang halos 0.24 kilometro kada oras.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang pinakahinay nga mammal?

Ang sloth! Molihok lang kini og halos 0.24 kilometro kada oras.

copy.tl: Ang slow loris ay isang nokturnal na hayop mula sa Asya na marahang gumagalaw sa mga puno kapag gabi.
copy.bis: Ang slow loris usa ka nokturnal nga mananap gikan sa Asya nga hinay molihok sa mga kahoy sa gabii.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A slug is basically like a snail, except it has no outer shell at all.

assignedReviews.reason: The card only notes that slugs lack an outer shell compared to snails. It does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their roles in movement or food gathering, which are the focus of G3-L-4.

copy.en:
What makes a slug different from a snail?

A slug is basically like a snail, except it has no outer shell at all.
copy.tl:
Ano ang kaiba ng slug sa suso?

Ang slug ay parang suso, pero wala itong panlabas na bahay o kabibi.
copy.bis:
Unsay lahi sa slug gikan sa suso?

Ang slug daw sama sa suso, apan wala kini gawas nga kabhang o bahay.
